title: Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction Act of 2018
official_summary:
Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction Act of 2018

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) a Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction Office, headed by an Assistant Secretary. The Assistant Secretary shall serve as the principal advisor to DHS on weapons of mass destruction matters and strategies, and on coordinating efforts to counter weapons of mass destruction.

The office shall coordinate DHS strategy and policy to plan, detect, and protect against the importation, possession, storage, transportation, development, or use of unauthorized chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear materials, devices, or agents.

The Assistant Secretary shall establish the Securing the Cities program to detect and prevent terrorist attacks and other high consequence events utilizing nuclear or other radiological materials that pose a high risk to homeland security in high-risk urban areas.

The bill establishes in the office a Chief Medical Officer who shall serve as the principal advisor to DHS on medical and public health issues.

DHS shall transfer to the office all personnel, budget authority, and assets of the Domestic Nuclear Detection Office and the Office of Health Affairs.

summary.headline: This law creates a new Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction Office inside the Department of Homeland Security and moves some existing offices into it.
summary.what_it_does: The law amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to set up a Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction Office at DHS, led by an Assistant Secretary who advises the department on weapons of mass destruction issues. The office coordinates DHS plans to prevent, detect, and protect against unauthorized chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear materials and devices. It requires a Securing the Cities program to detect nuclear or radiological threats in high-risk urban areas, and it creates a Chief Medical Officer to advise DHS on medical and public health matters. DHS must also transfer the personnel, budget, and assets of the Domestic Nuclear Detection Office and the Office of Health Affairs to the new office.

who_it_affects.group: Employees of the Domestic Nuclear Detection Office and the Office of Health Affairs
who_it_affects.how: Their positions, budgets, and assets are moved into the new Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction Office.
They become the focus of the Securing the Cities program, which is designed to detect nuclear or radiological threats.
It must set up the new office, appoint an Assistant Secretary and a Chief Medical Officer, and coordinate weapons of mass destruction strategy through the office.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on December 21, 2018; the summary does not give a separate effective date for the office's creation or the transfers.
